answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (titled 'NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout'), with quoted statements from Sharon AI's CEO and Firmus Technologies' co-CEO relayed in the same post.
answer.note: Material source claim: NVIDIA says it is introducing a new business model under which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, supported by revenue-sharing and credit-support terms. NVIDIA says it would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity. This is a self-described plan and model, not a reported financial result, so it supports the business description and intended revenue structure of NVIDIA rather than any achieved revenue. Conditional interpretation: if implemented at scale, the model could add a usage-linked revenue stream on top of product sales and could accelerate NVIDIA platform adoption among AI-native customers, but the size, timing and terms of that effect are not disclosed. The Firmus figures (campus expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) are expected capacity from NVIDIA's statement, not confirmed build status or confirmed NVIDIA orders. The Sharon AI quote and the statement that AI cloud companies are building DSX AI factories show partner activity, but the post does not give contract values or signing status.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, the scope of the credit-support commitment, and the financial terms of the model are not disclosed, so the size of any NVIDIA revenue or obligation cannot be estimated from this source.
No signing status is disclosed for the Sharon AI, Firmus or other partner arrangements; this is unknown, not confirmed as signed or unsigned.
The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are expectations stated in NVIDIA's post, with no completion date, build status or independent verification.
The source is a company self-description of its own model; the claim of earnings structure and adoption benefits is NVIDIA's view and is not corroborated by independent records here.
No historical records or catalog questions were supplied, so comparison against prior NVIDIA statements on this model is not possible.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's subsequent 10-Q or 10-K filings for disclosure of the revenue-sharing or credit-support arrangements, their accounting treatment, and any amounts or contingent obligations.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI press releases or filings for signed agreements, capacity schedules, financing and the status of the Batam campus build.
Check whether NVIDIA discloses credit-support exposure or guarantees tied to AI cloud partners in later financial statement footnotes.
Check NVIDIA earnings calls for quantification of the usage-linked revenue stream and how it is reported across product and cloud revenue.
